newsitem.title: USA: TRW says has China telecom satellite deal.
newsitem.headline: TRW says has China telecom satellite deal.

text.p: TRW Inc said Friday that China's Telecommunications Ministry had signed a memo of understanding to be a provider of cellular telephone services for the Odyssey satellite system, which TRW is building.

TRW did not disclose terms but a TRW spokesman said in a telephone interview the deal is significant for TRW. TRW and Canada's Teleglobe Inc are founding shareholders of Odyssey Telecommunications International Inc.
In a statement issued in Beijing, TRW said Odyssey expects to have 200,000 subscribers across China by 2002 and 1.3 million by 2010 for wireless and mobile telephone service.
At present, China is estimated to have one telephone for every 100 of its 1.2 billion people, TRW said. The patented $3.2 billion Odyssey system will begin service in 2001, it said.
The China agreement will allow subscribers across China to use a pocket-sized mobile phone or a fixed wireless phone to call anywhere on Earth, TRW said.
ChinaSat (China's Telecommunications Broadcast Satellite Corp) will be the exclusive distributor in China of Odyssey-based cellular phone, fax and data services, TRW said.
ChinaSat will also operate one of Odyssey's seven regional earth stations and own one or more gateways that connect the system to China's wireline and wireless infrastructure.
A subsidiary of the Post and Telecommunications Ministry, ChinaSat also administers other telecommunications and television transmission services.

"We believe Odyssey, working in partnership with ChinaSat, can deliver the highest quality mobile satellite services at the best price to Chinese consumers, especially in remote areas, and play a significant role in meeting China's ambitious development goals," TRW President Peter Hellman said in the statement.
